mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate crosses above 4% but S&P 500 returns remain positive, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI increases and federal funds rate is high, inflationary pressures may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPI increases and FEDFUNDS are high but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle recovery, increasing housing starts indicate economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase in early-cycle but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates strong economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production rises but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real consumer spending signals weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: If real consumer spending drops but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If employment rises but unemployment also increases, it may indicate labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If employment and unemployment both increase but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If federal funds rate is high but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis is rejected.
